analysis: Examined SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift (base vs head) and the recency tests. The only behavioral change is in scanOnDisk (head lines 149-165) and removeCorrupt (head 112-123). The TTL-expiry check is split from the header and metadata validation guard. An expired file is now deleted through the new private removeFile(tag) and is not counted as corruptDropped. removeFile uses the same code as before: performIndexedRemoval, which checks ownsEvictionRoot under removalLock, then removeItemIfSafe(under: root), then index.remove. Expired files are still unlinked and never inserted into the index, so the T-041 TTL bound (30-minute sliding TTL, enforced on scan) is unchanged. The scan still holds the fileCoordinator access while it removes. Validation (weightHash, layoutEpoch, blockSize, lookupTag prefix) still precedes any index insert, and failures still go to removeCorrupt, so the stats counter now distinguishes corruption from expiry. Nothing here changes crypto, HMAC naming, salt scoping, epoch handling or the capability advertisement. The cache epoch is not rotated by either path, which matches the documented T-041 posture. A residual edge: removeFile can return nil without deleting if ownsEvictionRoot is false. This was already true of removeCorrupt in base, so it is not a regression. The new tests cover non-corrupt expiry and corrupt-at-startup counting, with no security impact. No new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption found. Unchanged callers were not retrieved; the effect of corruptDropped stat semantics on any telemetry consumers is unverified but not security-relevant.
